The Gilt PressVol. IV · No. 2

Illuminated openings

The Letter That Earned Its Gold

In the old scriptoria, the first letter of a story was left grey until the very end — gilded last, as a reward for finishing the page.

E. VaneIllustrated openings · 6 min

Once, every book began with a small ceremony. The scribe would write the whole page in plain ink, leaving the first letter grey and unadorned, and only when the last line was dry would the gilder arrive with gold leaf and a steady hand. As it enters the view, it earns its colour: the grey warms, a band of light passes across the serif, and a vine draws itself beneath the opening line.

The effect is pure progressive enhancement. Without scripts the paragraph is simply a paragraph; with them, the opening letter is wrapped, floated, and gilded the first time it enters the viewport. The sweep and the vine are paint-only transitions, so the page never shifts beneath your thumb.

Readers who prefer reduced motion see the finished state at once — the gilded cap, the drawn vine — with nothing moving on its own. The decoration is hidden from assistive technology, and the words themselves are never touched.

A second telling, in copper

The same component, re-themed with custom properties: copper instead of gold, a higher scroll threshold before it gilds. Each opening on the page fires exactly once, the moment enough of its paragraph is visible, and then rests — calm, finished, and cheap when idle.

drop-cap-gilt · vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no build step · copy the folder, add data-drop-cap to any opening paragraph.

# drop-cap-gilt An illuminated-manuscript drop cap for article openings. The first letter of a paragraph stands about four lines tall in ink-grey serif; when the paragraph scrolls into view, a gold gradient sweeps across the letter once and a thin hand-drawn vine draws itself beneath the first line. Colour earned: the cap starts grey and gilds as the payoff. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. No build step, no framework, no dependencies. Copy the folder, include the CSS and the module, done. ## Markup ```html

Once upon a time…

``` The module auto-starts on every `[data-drop-cap]` element. The paragraph should begin with the letter (an opening quote is allowed and gilds with it). The vine stretches from just past the cap to the paragraph's right edge; it is absolutely positioned, so it reserves no space and the animation causes no layout shift. For manual control: ```js import { init } from './drop-cap-gilt.js'; // (also exported as dropCapGilt) const destroy = init(document.querySelector('p'), { threshold: 0.5 }); // destroy() removes listeners, observers, and everything added to the DOM, // restoring the paragraph's original text. ``` ## Options | Option | Attribute | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `threshold` | `data-threshold` | `0.35` | Fraction of the paragraph that must be visible to trigger gilding. Options object wins over the attribute. | Gilding fires exactly once per element. ## Theming Custom properties, all with fallbacks (factory tokens `--serif`, `--ink-2` are honoured when present): | Property | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `--dcg-size` | `5.6em` | Cap font-size (≈4 lines tall at 1.55 body leading) | | `--dcg-ink` | `--ink-2` / `#4a4744` | Cap colour before gilding | | `--dcg-gold` | `#b98a1e` | Gilded gold | | `--dcg-gold-light` | `#f0d489` | Sheen band that sweeps across | | `--dcg-gold-deep` | `#7c5f14` | Shadow edge of the gold | | `--dcg-vine` | gold-deep | Vine stroke and leaf colour | | `--dcg-vine-height` | `14px` | Vine strip height | | `--dcg-duration` | `1.8s` | Gold sweep time | | `--dcg-vine-duration` | `1.4s` | Vine draw time | | `--dcg-vine-delay` | `.45s` | Vine draw delay after the sweep starts | | `--dcg-ease` | `cubic-bezier(.33, 0, .2, 1)` | Easing for both | On browsers without `background-clip: text`, the cap cross-fades from grey to gold instead of sweeping. No convention rules were broken. ## Accessibility - The paragraph text is never altered: screen readers read the intact sentence, and the cap is an ordinary inline span. - The vine SVG is `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`. - `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` shows the finished gilded state immediately; nothing animates or moves by itself. - No keyboard interaction (the piece is decorative, not interactive). ## Credits No images, no third-party code. The vine is an original hand-plotted SVG path; the serif is the host page's `--serif` (the demo uses Cormorant Garamond from Google Fonts).
